purpose: Independently rederive the frozen deep-AQUAL transition obstruction, compare it with primary AQUAL, RAQUAL, and k-essence literature, and decide whether it is a standalone publication candidate without using the field-theory obstruction to reject static AQUAL phenomenology.

notation_map.our_invariant: X=-g^munu*d_mu(phi)*d_nu(phi)/2; quasistatic gradients have X<0 and homogeneous timelike gradients have X>0.
notation_map.deep_branch: mu(s)=f'(s)=A*s^p with A>0 and p=1/2 for exact deep AQUAL.
notation_map.principal_coefficients: C=mu and H=mu+2s*dmu/ds=(1+2p)*mu, equivalent up to the frozen sign/rescaling convention to C=P_X and K=P_X+2X*P_XX.

independent_benchmarks.expected: s=-2X maps the RAQUAL effective metric eigenvalues to the frozen C and K coefficients up to a positive normalization.
For every p>0, C, H, and det tend to zero as s approaches zero from the quasistatic side.
For 0<p<1, dmu/ds diverges at s=0; exact p=1/2 deep AQUAL is not C2 across the transition.
At p=1/2 the longitudinal-to-transverse principal ratio H/C is exactly two.
C_reg=sqrt(mu0^2+A^2*s) has C_reg(0)=H_reg(0)=mu0>0 and approaches A*sqrt(s) only asymptotically.
The quasistatic relative error is sqrt(1+1/t)-1 for t=A^2*s/mu0^2 and therefore cannot vanish at finite transition t=0.
The matched timelike extension has c_phi^2=1+A^2*X/mu0^2>1 for every X>0 relative to the conformal matter cone.
Independent log-slope probes recover p, 4p, and the p<1 derivative divergence while regulator probes retain both transition repair and finite accuracy cost.
